text:
maya: quick note — thinking about a quieter handoff model for dedicated->hosted overflow. current spillover feels noisy for tenants; we should consider a sandboxed path with softer quotas before full spillover.

eric: curious what you mean by "sandboxed" — traffic trickle or separate routing lane?

maya: separate lane that uses lower SLAs, rate-limited bursts, and optional telemetry tags so we can trace without changing tenant isolation flags. basically a shadow pool that only serves when dedicated is drained but doesn't immediately mark requests as "hosted" in billing reports.

raj: i like the idea. key question: billing and data boundary constraints. some customers explicitly forbid hitting hosted at all. how do we enforce opt-out?

li: we could add a per-tenant console toggle: `allow_quiet_overflow: true|false`. default false for enterprise tiers. that avoids surprise.

maya: yep — console flag + API pin. If opt-in, quota consumption is recorded to a sandbox bucket and visible in console as "overflow-sandbox usage" so charges (if any) are explicit.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/overflow-sandbox-api -> staging in 2m :rocket:

eric: operationally, we need eviction hysteresis. prefer `drain_threshold` + `backoff` so tenants aren't flipped back-and-forth. e.g.,
```json
{"drain_threshold":0.85, "backoff_sec":300, "max_trickle_qps":10}
```

raj: also need telemetry tags so dashboards can separate these requests from normal hosted calls. path: `route.source=sandbox-overflow`, `route.variant=kv-quantized` etc.

maya: agree. add a console toggle to surface sandbox traffic per model variant and region. UX note: show reason (capacity, region-congestion, manual) and a link to rollback policy.

sasha: what about model variant compatibility? we sometimes fallback to smaller quantized variants on hosted which changes outputs. customers might see semantic drift. need an explicit "variant-fallback policy" per tenant with levels: `strict`, `compatible`, `best_effort`.

li: propose default `compatible` means only variants with same architecture + validated eval pass. `best_effort` allows more aggressive quantization. `strict` rejects overflow unless exact model available.

eric: for telemetry and regression alerts we should tie sandbox traffic to eval sets. if sandboxed responses degrade by >X% on key prompts, send an automatic rollback and notify SRE/product.

maya: plus a rollout UX: when toggling `allow_quiet_overflow` in console, show an inline checklist: quota impact, variant policy, billing bucket, alert hooks. make it a one-click opt-in with a modal.

raj: security ask: make sure sandboxed path never writes to customer-managed KMS keys used by private deploys. i.e., denylist tenant keys for the sandbox lane.

li: technical note: simpler to treat sandbox pool as hosted but with no access to private KMS and with data retention TTL of X hours for trace logs.

maya: next steps: i'll mock console wireframes + schema for `overflow_policy` and share in #eng-platform-design. can folks comment on eviction/backoff defaults and variant policy enumerations?

eric: +1. suggest drain_threshold default 0.9, backoff 600s, max_trickle_qps relative to tenant commit.

raj: +1 from compliance side with opt-in and KMS denylist.

li: i can prototype API changes today, will push an RFC by EOD.

maya: thanks team. i'll follow up with draft RFC and wireframes. :thumbsup:
